performance.card.failuresTip: Agent API requests that didn’t succeed, by kind. Real errors: something went wrong in Combwork (a server error). Refused by a rule: a workflow rule or a guard said no and said what to do instead (a submit with nothing new, a move the rules don’t allow, no access); that is the workflow working, not a fault. Wrong calls: a bad argument, an unknown card, a missing file. Not sorted: recorded before Combwork sorted failures. Cancelled requests aren’t counted here.

performance.stalls.heading: Main process stalls
performance.stalls.tip: Times Combwork's main process was busy for more than 250 ms. Every pane's typing goes through it, so a stall is felt as lag. Step is the work that held it, where Combwork knows it (a database or file step); During it is what else was under way, which may only have waited behind it. Little CPU means it was waiting (on the disk, a lock, another program); it is measured from half a second before, so it can be a little more than the length. The last {kept, number} since Combwork started, kept in memory only; combwork.log notes them too, at most one line a minute.
performance.toolList.heading: Combwork tool list
performance.toolList.tip: The Combwork tools’ names, descriptions and schemas as each session’s CLI got them, once a start, on average, by provider (Unknown: starts from before Combwork recorded it). Characters are the list’s JSON; Descriptions and Parameters are the tools’ descriptions and their parameters’ descriptions in it; Schemas is the rest: names, types, keys, punctuation and escapes. Up front is what the CLI puts in the prompt at the start: Claude Code defers MCP tools, so its model sees their names, and in full only the few Combwork marks; it loads another’s definition when it uses it, which isn’t observable. Codex and Copilot get the whole list. Either way the list sits at the start of the prompt, so it is cached after the first turn. A dash: not measured (sessions from before Combwork measured it).
performance.toolList.upfrontTip: What the CLI puts in the prompt at the start: for Claude Code, which defers MCP tools, the tools Combwork marks to be sent in full and the others’ names (its own wording of them isn’t observable); for Codex and Copilot, the whole list. A dash: not known.
